title_en: Reply of the Supreme People's Court on Whether a Victim in a Product Infringement Case May File a Civil Lawsuit against the Trademark Owner of the Product as Defendant

articles.content_en:
(Amended in accordance with the Decision of the Supreme People's Court on Amending Nineteen Civil Action Judicial Interpretations, including the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning Civil Mediation Work of the People's Courts, adopted at the 1823rd Session
of the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court on December 23, 2020)
Beijing Higher People's Court:
We have received your court's Report Requesting Instructions on the Results of Handling the Issue of Determining Litigation Subjects in the Damage Compensation Case of Jing Qilian, Zhang Xinrong, et al. v. General Motors Corporation and General Motors Overseas Corporation (Jing Gao Fa [2001] No. 271). Upon study, we are of the opinion that any enterprise or individual that places its own personal name, appellation, trademark, or other identifiable mark on a product to indicate that it is the manufacturer of the product shall be deemed a "manufacturer" as provided in the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China and the Product Quality Law of the People's Republic of China. In this case, General Motors Corporation is the owner of the trademark on the accident vehicle. Based on the victims' prosecution and the actual circumstances of this case, it is not improper to name General Motors Corporation, General Motors Overseas Corporation, and General Motors do Brasil as defendants in this case.
